rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The `**What happened:**` block is OPTIONAL, default omit; when included, three moves (count+noun, one qualifier, land on destination), 1-3 sentences, 25-40 words.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 89 (raw): '**What happened:** A one-screen gap map across memory / verifier / skill, one stale rule cut in place, and a diagrammed map of the work that recurs across your stack. The shapes stay in this session's scrollback; you build the handoff prompt from them.' Word count of the block body (excluding the label) = 42 words, over the rule's stated 25-40 ceiling by 2. On move 3: the sentence names a consumer ('you build the handoff prompt from them'), which the rule's own examples permit ('what reads it next' is a legal alternative to naming a location) — so the move is not absent. But 'the handoff prompt' is never established anywhere else in this file's body; nothing upstream produces, names, or previews a 'handoff prompt', so the reader reaches a noun with no anchor and no way to verify the forward pointer is real. That is weaker than the rule's own worked examples ('living in your personal skills folder. Shipped.', 'the artifact STRIDE reads next'), which each name a concrete, already-legible destination or a named external reader. Net: move 3 is present in shape but not fully doing its job — it gestures forward without giving the reader anything to hold, which is close to (if short of) the fictional-gate failure `check_student_facing.md`'s fifth axis warns about for headings/bullets asserting a thing that turns out unanchored.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut to the word ceiling and anchor 'the handoff prompt' to something already established in this file (or drop the forward reference and let the block end on the artifact list) rather than naming an unintroduced downstream noun.
